2026-10-22 asr-quality T-ASRQ-04: canonical transcript segments carry confidence = exp(min(0, avg_logprob)) x (1 - no_speech_prob) of their raw segments, a 0-1 review hint rounded to three decimals. A projected segment keeps its raw value weighted by its owned (clipped) duration; cross-window duplicates and fully trimmed boundary fragments fold into the kept cue as a duration-weighted mean, and an overlap repair reweights the moved cue by its adjusted span. Timing, text, merge, shaping, retry and quality decisions are unchanged; the field is optional in the transcript schema, so older transcripts stay valid. The legacy-parity replay strips only this reviewed field. 2026-10-23 asr-quality T-ASRQ-11: after the cross-window merge the post-processor reports window seam duplicates in report.seamDuplicates (cue ids, times, seam, clipped edge, coverage and kept cue ids; no text): a cue whose raw observation straddled an overlapping core seam and was clipped to it, when it has at least 2 CJK or 4 Latin comparison characters (NFKC, lowercase, without punctuation and whitespace) and the fewest insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn them into one contiguous stretch of the cues across the seam whose raw observations overlap its own (joined in time order) are at most 20% of them, reported as coverage = (characters - edits) / characters; the next window's clipped cue is judged first and a dropped cue is never compared again. A cue that already keeps an earlier reported duplicate is reported only when that duplicate still reaches 80% with its remaining kept cues, and that entry then lists only those, so a kept cue is never reported across consecutive seams. The canonical transcript and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged; the exported dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates removes a reported cue only while it and its kept cues keep their reported timing and wording (separators aside) and none of its kept cues is removed with it. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-11 review: the seam comparison is local (closest contiguous stretch) instead of a whole-text in-order common subsequence, so a short reply whose characters only occur apart in a longer cue across the seam is no longer reported; every earlier T-ASRQ-11 case keeps its decision and coverage. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-11 refinement after the real-audio rerun: (1) far-end guard: a clipped cue is not reported when at least 2 CJK or 4 Latin of its comparison characters at its far end (away from the seam: the end of a next-window cue, the start of a previous-window cue) have no counterpart in the closest stretch across the seam, counting only the trailing characters that no fewest-edit alignment pairs with any character across the seam, matched or substituted (so only characters past the end of the other side's text count, and far-end characters that merely differ still count toward the coverage), so a copy the other window stops short of keeps its words; the previous window's clipped fragment that the kept copy fully covers is then judged and reported in the previous-window pass. Edits elsewhere still count toward the 80% coverage, and judging an earlier decision again applies the same guard. (2) Edge restore: an entry may carry restoredEdge {cueId, edge, fromMs, toMs} (no text) naming its kept cue that is clipped to the same seam on the opposite edge (start of a next-window kept cue, end of a previous-window kept cue); toMs is its raw edge, never past the reported cue's far edge, capped by maxCueDurationMs against the other edge (an end against the start already restored at the cue's earlier seam, since seams are judged in time order) and omitted when no move remains; an entry whose restored cue a later decision reports loses it. dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates moves that edge only together with the drop (all kept cues unchanged), never over the nearest remaining cue on that side, never changes text, and returns each dropped entry with the edge it actually restored or without restoredEdge. The canonical transcript and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged.
